summary: This continuation reconstructs overconvergent F-isocrystals from their extremal slope data. It develops bounded quotients, PBQ filtrations and saturation over local analytic fields and curves, connects these to dagger hulls and the minimal slope property, and uses Lefschetz curves over finite fields. It separates existence of an isomorphism from lifting a prescribed quotient map and records the precise inputs each assertion needs.

nodes.title: Generic bounded solutions
nodes.statement: For a finite (φ,∇)-module M/E, pull back through τ:E→E[[u]]₀, τ(a)=Σ ∂^i(a)u^i/i!. Define Solη(M)=Hom∇(τ*M,E{u}), with E{u} the analytic functions on the open unit disc, and Solη,0(M)=Hom∇(τ*M,E[[u]]₀). nodes.title: Maximally bounded quotient
nodes.statement: A (φ,∇)-module over E is bounded when its Taylor realisation is trivial over E[[u]]₀. Let Mᵇ be the unique least differential submodule whose quotient is bounded. Equivalently M/Mᵇ is the universal bounded quotient; Mᵇ is the common annihilator of Solη,0(M) under evaluation. Write B(M)=M/Mᵇ; zero has B(0)=0.

nodes.title: Bounded splitting theorem
nodes.statement: Over E with perfect coefficient residue k, M is bounded iff its increasing slope filtration splits as a direct sum of pure differential Frobenius modules. In particular every pure object is bounded; for nonzero M its maximal pure slope quotient is nonzero and bounded.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: For a pure module use a Frobenius-stable unit-root lattice after an allowed slope twist and the generic Taylor estimates (Ohkubo Proposition 5.9, p.26).
For bounded M apply bounded-extension-splitting to successive pure slope grades, normalising the smallest slope first. The off-diagonal analytic cases, including gap one, are essential.
Descend the unique distinct-slope splittings and induct through the filtration. This proves differential splitting, rather than just a splitting after forgetting the connection.
acceptance: A nontrivial extension between distinct slopes need not be bounded merely because it is solvable.

nodes.title: PBQ filtration
nodes.statement: There is a unique filtration 0=P₀M⊂P₁M⊂⋯⊂P_rM=M whose successive nonzero grades G_i=P_iM/P_(i−1)M are PBQ with strictly decreasing λ_i=λmax(G_i). P₁M is the largest PBQ subobject of maximal slope λmax(M), and subsequent terms are obtained from that construction on the quotient. For M=0 the length is zero.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. proofSteps: First construct a nonzero PBQ subobject of maximal slope: take the preimage in M of the maximal pure summand of B(M). If this preimage is PBQ use it; otherwise it is proper and induction on rank supplies its maximal PBQ subobject (CT11 Proposition 5.4, p.56).

Sum PBQ subobjects of this fixed maximal slope, using the quotient criterion and finite length, to obtain the unique largest one. The next quotient has strictly smaller maximal slope, so induction gives the filtration.
Compare the unique first term and apply induction to the quotient to prove uniqueness.

A nonzero pure object has one step.
For L_1⊕L_0 of slopes 1 and 0, grades have slopes 1 then 0; the nested second term still has maximal slope 1.

nodes.title: Interior and boundary gluing
nodes.statement: For affine C with smooth completion C̄, a generic differential Frobenius submodule Lη⊂Mη comes from a unique dagger subobject of M† if it has compatible saturated bounded-disc submodules at every point of C and compatible E† boundary submodules at every point of C̄∖C. nodes.title: Bounded extension splitting
nodes.statement: Let 0→L→M→Q→0 be an exact sequence over E with pure L,Q of slopes a,b. It splits as differential Frobenius modules if b<a, or b−a>1, or M is bounded and 0<b−a≤1. Bounded splitting of arbitrary slope filtrations follows by induction; the two latter cases are the analytic content, not a consequence of solvability.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: For b<a solve the off-diagonal Frobenius equation by a contracting inverse and use slope-Hom vanishing to make the splitting horizontal.

After allowed coefficient extension and Taylor change, take σ(t)=t^q and normalise the diagonal blocks. For b−a>1 compare the off-diagonal Frobenius–connection identity and coefficient orders to force both off-diagonal blocks to vanish.

For 0<b−a<1, a surviving off-diagonal block yields an unbounded generic Taylor solution; at b−a=1 treat the connection block first and obtain an exact growth-one solution. Boundedness excludes these. Unique distinct-slope splittings descend under the allowed extensions.
acceptance: The small positive-gap case requires bounded M; dropping this condition would rule out the logarithmic nonsplit examples.
